us-house.budget-law-tax: a budget law lowering national tax revenue by about 1.25 percent of annual economic output a year for ten years, mostly through making permanent expiring lower tax rates on earnings and on business income, lifting the tax-free amount of inherited wealth, and adding deductions for tips and for overtime pay through 2028
us-house.overdraft-rule-repeal: a repeal of a rule that was to cap, at a low fixed amount or at cost, the fees large banks and credit unions charge when an account is overdrawn. About one in six households pay such fees, according to the regulator's figures
us-house.federal-bargaining-bill: a bill to return collective bargaining rights to national government employees in the agencies where orders from the head of government had ended them. According to government data, the union-represented share of national government employees fell from about 56 to about 38 percent in the year those orders took effect

uk-commons.finance-law-2025: a finance law raising the tax rates on investment gains, charging sales tax on private school fees, raising the extra tax paid when buying a second home, and replacing a rule under which some long-term residents could avoid tax on income kept abroad, which raises tax revenue by about 0.15 percent of annual economic output by 2030
uk-commons.finance-law-2026: a finance law freezing income tax thresholds for three more years, lifting tax rates on income from dividends, savings, and property by 2 points, and bringing unused pension savings and more farm and business assets into inheritance tax, which raises tax revenue by about 0.35 percent of annual economic output by 2030
uk-commons.employment-rights-law: a law giving employees protection from unfair dismissal once they have six months of service, not two years, paying sick pay from the first day someone is ill, granting workers on variable hours a right to guaranteed hours, limiting the dismissal and rehiring of staff on worse terms, and loosening rules on union organizing and strikes. The government estimated that about 60 percent of workers gain new rights under it

de-bundestag.investment-tax-law: a law reducing the tax rate on company profits by 5 points step by step from 2028 to 2032, from about 30 to about 25 percent with local taxes included, and letting firms deduct investment costs faster until 2027. The official estimate of its cost is up to about 0.25 percent of annual economic output a year
de-bundestag.tax-amendment-law: a tax law cutting the sales tax on restaurant meals for good from 19 to 7 percent and raising the deduction allowed for commuting costs. The official estimate of its cost is about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year
de-bundestag.procurement-pay-law: a law under which companies doing national government contracts above a set value must provide their workers the pay and conditions set by the relevant collective agreements. By the government's count there are about 16,000 such contracts a year

fr-assemblee.budget-2025: an annual budget passed with no vote on its text, which created a temporary surtax on the profits of some 400 companies with the largest revenue and set a minimum 20 percent tax rate for the highest incomes, raising tax revenue by about 0.3 percent of annual economic output
fr-assemblee.budget-2026: the next year's budget, again passed with no vote on its text, which extended the same surtax for a second year to a smaller set of companies and added a 20 percent tax on luxury assets owned through family holding companies. The surtax's yield is about 0.25 percent of annual economic output, by an unofficial estimate
fr-assemblee.wealth-floor-bill: a bill for a minimum annual tax equal to 2 percent of wealth on fortunes worth more than about 500 times the median household's wealth, which the lower chamber passed and the upper chamber rejected. Its yield was estimated at about 0.1 percent of annual economic output by a legislative committee and at about 0.7 percent by its author

ca-commons.income-tax-cut: a law reducing the lowest rate of income tax from 15 to 14 percent. The official estimate of its cost is about 0.15 percent of annual economic output a year, with the savings growing in amount as income rises, up to the second bracket
ca-commons.budget-law-investment: a budget law letting businesses write off the cost of new investment faster. The official estimate of its cost is about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year across five years
